My forecast indicates a gradual upward trend in the point estimates over time, moving from 151.75 for tomorrow, to 152.36 in a week, and 153.87 in a month. It implies that, absent any major disruptions, the general trajectory is expected to be slightly upward.

The most noticeable feature of this forecast is the widening of the 90% confidence intervals as the time horizon extends. This expansion directly reflects the increasing uncertainty inherent in forecasting further into the future. Essentially, while we might have a good idea of immediate movement, the range of plausible outcomes expands considerably as time progresses.

While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain specific, high-impact risks or events could still push the actual value outside these stated bounds. These might include sudden and significant shifts in economic policy, unforeseen geopolitical events that disrupt global markets or supply chains, a major technological breakthrough or catastrophic failure, or an abrupt and dramatic change in market sentiment driven by unexpected news. Events such as a severe natural disaster, a rapid onset of a recession, or a completely unanticipated regulatory change could fundamentally alter the underlying conditions and cause the value to deviate substantially from even the outer limits of my predicted ranges.
